newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad R'dam's Amersfoortse raises '96 net.
newsitem.headline: Stad R'dam's Amersfoortse raises '96 net.

text.p: Amersfoortse Verzekeringsgroep NV, a unit of insurer Stad Rotterdam, said on Monday its 1996 net profit had risen by 15.8 percent to 61.6 million guilders.
Turnover grew by 11.5 percent to 1.16 billion guilders.
For 1997 further growth of profits and turnover is expected, the company said.

Stad Rotterdam is currently taking over the 45 percent in Amersfoortse it does not already own. In April it said it expected to reach agreement with Muenchener Rueckversicherung and Nuernberger Beteiligungs AG to buy their stakes in Amersfoortse of 25 and 20 percent respectively.

After the deal, which will be partly financed through issuing new Stad Rotterdam shares, Muenchener Rueckversicherung will hold an interest of about 12 percent in the new combination of Stad Rotterdam and Amersfoortse.
Amersfoortse previously said it expected its 1996 net profit to rise by about 15 percent to more than 60 million guilders.

The company said premium income of its non-life insurance division had grown by 13.2 percent to 612.3 million guilders and accidents and health insurance had risen by 16.7 percent to 491.5 million guilders.
Premium income from car insurance grew by 3.5 percent to 83.1 percent. After a number of previous losses, this sector posted a positive result for the first time in years.
But Amersfoortse said there was fierce competition in the car insurance sector so that the recovery of profitability in this area may already be running out of steam.
Life insurance income rose by 5.5 percent to 323.9 million guilders. Production of new life insurance grew to a record level of 1.6 billion.
Amersfoortse said its 1996 investment income had increased by 16 percent to 227.3 million guilders. Its investment portfolio totalled almost 3.5 billion guilders, about 0.5 million more than in 1995.
The company's shareholders' equity was raised by 17.4 percent to 386.2 million guilders by the end of 1996.
